name: issue-grinder
description: Deliver selected Task Manager scope through five execution modes and answer mode-help questions without starting delivery.

interface.shortDescription: Grind selected Task Manager issues to verified outcomes.
interface.longDescription: Includes two independent Task Manager skills. Issue Grinder delivers an explicit issue, Release, Project, or current-Release scope through To Do, In Progress, and In Review. It also answers pure questions about its modes, default resolver, differences, or selection through a delivery-free help path that does not access Task Manager, create a Goal, rename the task, or call subagents. It supports five stable execution modes: Solo keeps all Issue Grinder delivery work in one execution lane on the current top-level model while allowing bounded service-provider agents outside that topology; in Classic the controller does almost all work and gives Luna only trivial, strictly bounded packets; in Balance Luna is the preferred executor for light and medium bounded tasks, but preserves its checkpoint and evidence and returns problems to the controller for fallback; Swarm runs isolated candidate and critic waves before reducing them to one exact candidate; Economical maximizes safe progress and may leave one honest resumable checkpoint instead of claiming completion. Solo is selected explicitly and works with one or many issues; issue count alone does not select it. Without an explicit mode, any Luna top-level model selects Economical and any other model selects Classic; the decision is made once per continuous run. Mode topology includes only agents doing Issue Grinder delivery work; outer controllers and bounded semantic providers stay outside it unless they take on analysis, implementation, testing, technical review, candidate selection, or delivery decisions. It creates a strategic Goal only for an explicitly invoked multi-issue run, keeps live scope dynamic, treats blocked-by as an implementation-readiness gate, and requires human-readable comments for every non-trivial lifecycle transition. A candidate blocker must become a causal explanation and a fresh reflection over current primary sources; any verified safe in-scope action cancels the blocker and resumes work. A terminal handoff lists every confirmed blocking cause and gives a separate answer for each one explaining why it blocks the goal, why Issue Grinder cannot resolve it alone, and what the blocked step contributes to the goal. Public UAT and other confirmed non-production environments do not need routine approval, while Production remains forbidden. Independent writers and intentional candidates use separate feature branches and Git worktrees, one integration owner performs fan-in, and final acceptance applies to one exact integrated candidate. Task Composer remains planning-only and creates Task Manager Backlog scope without implementing it. Both skills use the separately installed Task Manager adapter. In all five modes Issue Grinder uses the standalone Strategic Explainer when available and otherwise writes natively; its provider remains outside mode execution topology while it handles only publication, and Explainer absence never blocks comments, status transitions, or final reporting.
defaultPrompt: Используй $issue-grinder, чтобы довести текущий Release в Task Manager до проверенного результата
Используй $issue-grinder, чтобы довести указанное issue до выхода из To Do, In Progress и In Review
Используй $issue-grinder:task-composer, чтобы оформить это требование в Task Manager Backlog
